source: Flavell (1979) Metacognition and cognitive monitoring
finding: Founding statement. Metacognitive knowledge is beliefs about person, task and strategy variables. Most of it is about interactions among them. It is ordinary long-term knowledge, not a special store. The paper has no data; it is a model.
numbers: No numbers. Cites Flavell 1970 on children failing to see the need for rehearsal.
quote: you should use Strategy A (rather than Strategy B) in Task X (as contrasted with Task Y)
limits: Theory paper. Declarative, procedural and conditional are Schraw's later labels, not Flavell's. Flavell's interaction idea is the conditional one.
agent_relevance: The class record is exactly a stored person x task x strategy interaction: use Strategy A in Task X. It is knowledge to be retrieved, which fits a lookup table.

source: Gutierrez de Blume & Montoya (2021) Spanish MAI in Colombian undergraduates (Psicogente)
finding: Large replication of the Metacognitive Awareness Inventory in Spanish. The two-factor model (knowledge, regulation) fits very well. The model that splits knowledge into declarative, procedural and conditional does not.
numbers: N=528. Two-factor CFA: CFI .96, RMSEA .05, loadings .58 to .92. Higher-order model with declarative/procedural/conditional under knowledge: CFI .84, RMSEA .11 (inadequate). First-order 8-factor model alone: CFI .93, RMSEA .06. Chi-square difference test favoured two factors.
limits: Self-report, university students, one country. Cannot tell if the three kinds of knowledge are distinct in behaviour, only that people do not report them as distinct.
agent_relevance: The three-way split is weak as a measured construct. Do not build three separate stores. One class record keyed by (class, operator) is enough; the declarative/procedural/conditional tag adds no tested value.

source: Harrison & Vallin (2018) Evaluating the MAI using empirical factor-structure evidence
finding: Best-known critique of the MAI. Score it as two dimensions (knowledge, regulation). The full 52-item form has poor fit. A 19-item subset fits and is invariant across groups.
numbers: N=622 undergraduates. CFA and multidimensional item-response modelling. 52 items poor fit; 19-item subset good fit; provisional longitudinal invariance.
limits: Seen as ERIC abstract only, not full text. Self-report.
agent_relevance: Same message as b02 from a US sample: two factors yes, eight or three-way knowledge split no.

source: Junior MAI 18-item factor structure study (ERIC record, 2017)
url: https://eric.ed.gov (Establishing the Factor Structure of the 18-Item Version of the Junior Metacognitive Awareness Inventory)
finding: Children's version of the MAI also supports two factors, knowledge and regulation of cognition.
numbers: Exploratory N=1,783 and confirmatory N=942, grades 6 to 12.
limits: Abstract only. Authors not checked.
agent_relevance: Two-factor structure is stable from grade 6 to adult. Knowledge about strategies is not separable from regulation at a finer level.

source: Arabic MAI short version study (ERIC record, 2024)
url: https://eric.ed.gov (Factor Structure of the Arabic Version of the MAI Short Version: Insights from Network Analysis)
finding: 19-item Arabic MAI: first- and second-order CFA confirmed two factors, but exploratory graph analysis found three dimensions, which differ from the CFA.
numbers: General population sample in Saudi Arabia; one item dropped for poor indexes; no gender invariance by delta-CFI and delta-RMSEA.
limits: Abstract only. Sample size not read.
agent_relevance: The dimensional structure depends on the method used. Treat any fixed number of knowledge types as a modelling choice.

source: Latvian, Russian and other MAI adaptations (search summary)
finding: Several translated MAIs failed to reproduce the original structure. A Russian version (N=527) fit none of four tested models until items were cut. A Latvian adaptation did not reproduce the original model.
numbers: Russian version N=527, four models tested, fit only after dropping items.
limits: Known only from a web-search summary, not opened. Exact fit indices unknown.
agent_relevance: Failed replications exist and are not rare. The inventory is not a clean measure of the three knowledge types.

source: Dignath & Buttner (2008) Components of fostering self-regulated learning: meta-analysis
finding: Self-regulated learning training raises achievement in school children. Effects are larger in primary than secondary school.
numbers: 84 studies (49 primary, 35 secondary), 357 effect sizes, mean effect size about 0.69 (from search summary).
limits: Numbers come from a search snippet, not the paper. Moderator values not verified. DOI not checked.
agent_relevance: Telling learners which strategy fits which task (the conditional part) is one of the trained components. Gains are real but trained by humans over weeks, not one prompt.

source: Donker et al. (2014) Effectiveness of learning strategy instruction on academic performance
finding: Strategy instruction improves performance, and the best strategy type depends on the subject. Instruction on metacognitive knowledge appeared useful in all domains.
numbers: 58 studies, primary and secondary education (from search summary). Effect sizes not verified.
limits: Snippet only. Do not quote effect sizes from this line.
agent_relevance: Supports a domain-specific record: what works depends on the class of task, as the agent assumes.

source: de Boer et al. (2018) Long-term effects of metacognitive strategy instruction: meta-analysis
finding: Metacognitive strategy instruction effects last. Follow-up effect is about the same as, or slightly above, the posttest effect.
numbers: 48 interventions; posttest Hedges g about 0.50 (abstract excerpt via search). One secondary blog quoted a follow-up g of 0.63; unverified.
limits: Snippet only. Heterogeneity and moderators not read.
agent_relevance: Stored strategy knowledge does not decay quickly once taught. A persistent class record is a reasonable design.

source: Didolkar et al. (2024) Metacognitive capabilities of LLMs: math problem solving
finding: GPT-4 named skills for each math problem, clustered them into a skill list, and used exemplars matched to the skill of a new question. This beat plain CoT and beat topic-matched exemplars.
numbers: MATH: about 5,000 raw skills clustered into 117. +11.6 points over CoT, +3.5 over Complex CoT and over topic-based exemplars. PAL code: +7.52 points on 500 MATH items. Transfer to Mixtral 8x7B (MATH): CoT+skill 28.44 vs topic 26.14; with maj@4 skill 32.44 vs topic 30.75.
limits: Skills named by GPT-4 and used on the same dataset. Transfer to other datasets and models is smaller. The skill label itself is the model's guess; the paper does not score its accuracy.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for a class record: label the problem class, then pull what worked for that class. The gain is from matching examples to the class, not from the label alone.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Self-Discover: LLMs self-compose reasoning structures
finding: The model picks reasoning modules from a list of 39, adapts them, and writes a task-level plan, then solves each instance with that plan. It beats CoT on tasks that need structure.
numbers: Accuracy (BBH / T4D / MATH). GPT-4: 58/51/70.5 plain; CoT 75/52/71; Self-Discover 81/85/73. PaLM 2-L: 56/30/45 plain; CoT 60/40/42; Self-Discover 67/69/50.5. Uses 10 to 40 times fewer inference calls than self-consistency. Of 200 error cases, 87.5% had a correct structure; 74.7% of MATH errors came from calculation, not structure.
limits: Gain is task-level, chosen once per task and not per instance. Math gain is small (1 to 3 points on GPT-4) because errors are computational.
agent_relevance: Choosing the operator is cheap and often right, but structure is not the main error source on calculation tasks. Operator choice helps most where CoT does not fit (T4D).

source: Gao et al. (2024) Meta-Reasoning Prompting (MRP)
finding: The model chooses one of seven reasoning methods from short descriptions, then applies it. With GPT-4 it gives the best average. With GPT-3.5 it does not: the weaker model picks poorly.
numbers: GPT-4 macro average over 7 tasks: MRP 0.772, ToT 0.725, SPP 0.688, Self-Refine 0.677, CoT 0.654. GPT-3.5 macro average: SPP 0.469, STEP-BACK 0.452, Analogical 0.433, MRP 0.433, CoT 0.416. GPT-4 Game of 24: MRP 0.31 vs ToT 0.41. BigToM: MRP 0.57 vs ToT 0.43.
limits: MRP did not win every task even with GPT-4 (Game of 24 went to ToT). Authors list scoring errors, self-opinion, factual and reasoning errors for GPT-3.5.
agent_relevance: Self-chosen strategy knowledge scales with model strength. On a weak model, a fixed best single method can beat self-selection. Our program should pick from a measured record, not ask the model.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Reasoning Strategies in LLMs: Can They Follow, Prefer, and Optimize?
finding: Models follow a requested reasoning strategy well, but when left free they do not pick better than a fixed strategy. No single strategy wins. An oracle that picks per problem would roughly double accuracy on TruthQuest. Simple ensembles recover part of it.
numbers: TruthQuest (2,400 items), accuracy: Phi-4 no-strategy 47.2% vs oracle 82.9%; R1-Distill 63.4% vs 90.1%. ZebraLogic: Phi-4 27.3% vs 37.7%; Qwen3-8B 32.0% vs 36.4%. Compliance with requested strategy (Phi-4): Supposition Following 99%, Chain Construction 61%, Compound 81%, Concatenation 55%; when not told, it uses Chain Construction only 12%. Merging: majority vote on Phi-4 TruthQuest 54.9% vs best single 49.0%; vote+prob 57.3%; verifier on R1-Distill 74.1% vs 63.4%.
limits: Logic puzzles only; four prompts per problem; oracle is an upper bound. No merging rule won everywhere.
agent_relevance: Strongest result for us: procedural knowledge (follows a strategy) is good, conditional knowledge (knows which to choose) is poor. The gap between 47% and 83% is the prize for a good class record.

source: Liu et al. (2024) SMART: Self-learning Meta-strategy Agent for Reasoning Tasks
finding: Training the model with reinforcement learning to pick among CoT, Least-to-Most and Program-of-Thought on the first attempt improves accuracy over the best fixed strategy. Gains shrink as the base model gets stronger.
numbers: GSM8K single pass: Gemma 7B +15.2 points (to 55.6); Mistral 7B +11.0 (to 67.9); Qwen2 7B +3.5 (to 85.4). After refinement: +16.2, +7.9, +1.5.
limits: Requires training, so it is not a prompt-only result. Three math strategies only. The table layout in the text extract was jumbled, so baselines were read from the stated deltas.
agent_relevance: Strategy choice can be learned from outcome, which is what a class record does without weights. The shrinking gain at 85% accuracy says the record matters most where the model is weak.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) AdaptThink: Reasoning models can learn when to think
finding: Choosing between thinking and not thinking by problem difficulty cuts cost and slightly raises accuracy. Always skipping thinking loses accuracy on hard sets.
numbers: R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B: response length -50.9% (GSM8K), -63.5% (MATH500), -44.7% (AIME24) with accuracy +4.1, +1.4, +1.6 points; average -53% length, +2.4% accuracy. Always-NoThinking: average accuracy -12.7 points, length -79.9%.
limits: Needs RL training. Math only. Small model.
agent_relevance: A difficulty-conditioned switch is a concrete, measured form of conditional knowledge. Cheap operator for easy items, expensive for hard.

source: Dong et al. (2025) Meta-R1: Empowering large reasoning models with metacognition
finding: A small meta-level model plans, monitors and stops the reasoning model. Beats vanilla and eight baselines on accuracy and tokens. Removing the strategy-selection stage lowers accuracy.
numbers: R1-Distill-Qwen-14B average over GSM8K, AIME24, MATH500: vanilla 84.0% at 5,691 tokens; Meta-R1 87.0% at 3,941 tokens. AIME24: 64.4 to 70.0. Ablation without stage 3 (strategy selection): GSM8K 94.5% at 650 tokens, MATH500 93.8% at 2,770, below the full model (95.9 and 94.5).
limits: Meta-level is a 1.5B to 3B model. Compared against tuned baselines, one benchmark triple. Ablation row for stage 1 is missing from the text; which backbone the ablation uses was not confirmed.
agent_relevance: A separate module that holds strategy knowledge and applies it from outside is better than the model judging itself. Matches our rule that the program decides.

source: Elenjical et al. (2026) Think2: Grounded metacognitive reasoning in LLMs
finding: Forcing Brown's plan-monitor-evaluate cycle on a model that was not trained for it hurts accuracy. On a reasoning-trained model it helps error diagnosis and self-correction. Human raters prefer the traces.
numbers: Llama-3-8B GSM8K: Ann Brown prompt 69.55% vs Standard 80.71% vs CoT 77.98%. Qwen-3-8B: GSM8K 91.65%; AIME 5.89% (best). Self-correction success 50.0% vs 25.0% for CoT; correct diagnosis 58.3% vs 27.9% (aggregate baselines). Strict error rate 4.1% vs 7.4% (p=0.0005 vs pooled baselines; not significant against CoT or zero-shot alone). Human preference 84.1% over 580 query pairs.
limits: 8B models, small samples per benchmark, human preference is not accuracy. Authors admit the structure degrades non-reasoning models.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: metacognitive structure helps only when the model can carry it. Do not run the full cycle on every item; route by difficulty.

source: Wang & Zhao (2023/2024) Metacognitive Prompting improves understanding in LLMs
finding: A five-step introspective prompt beats CoT on ten NLU datasets across four models, but it makes simple tasks worse by overthinking.
numbers: Zero-shot average relative gain 4.8% to 6.4% over CoT and 2.8% to 4.1% over plan-and-solve; 5-shot 4.5% to 6.0% over manual CoT. Examples: MedNLI 70.9 vs 67.1 (CoT), EUR-LEX 55.8 vs 48.8 (as read from a jumbled table). Errors: overthinking 68.3% (simple sets such as QQP, BoolQ), overcorrection 31.7% (WiC, DDI).
limits: NLU classification only, not reasoning. Gains are a few points. Same authors' prompt, no independent replication found.
agent_relevance: Same lesson as Think2: extra metacognition costs accuracy on easy classes. The record must say skip for easy classes.

source: Didolkar et al. (2025) Metacognitive Reuse: turning recurring reasoning into concise behaviors
finding: The model reads its own traces, writes short named behaviors (how-to hints), stores them in a handbook, and retrieves them later. Fewer tokens at the same accuracy, and better self-improvement than critique-and-revise.
numbers: Up to 46% fewer reasoning tokens at matched or better accuracy; up to 10% higher accuracy than naive critique-and-revise; behavior-conditioned SFT beats vanilla SFT.
limits: Math focus. Figures are up-to maxima. Behaviors are retrieved by the model, so retrieval quality is not isolated.
agent_relevance: This is procedural knowledge stored outside the weights, built from the agent's own runs. It is close to our class record in function.

source: Binder et al. (2024) Looking Inward: language models can learn about themselves by introspection
finding: After fine-tuning, a model predicts its own behavior better than a different model trained on its behavior. This works for simple properties and fails for harder or out-of-distribution ones.
numbers: GPT-4o average self-prediction accuracy rose from 32.6% to 49.4% after training. Self-prediction advantage over a cross-trained model about +17% (Llama-70B vs GPT-4o).
limits: Needs fine-tuning. Authors say the effect does not hold on more complex tasks. Not a test of strategy choice.
agent_relevance: Models have only narrow, trained access to what they would do. Do not rely on a model's own claim of which strategy it will use well.

source: Steyvers et al. (2025) What LLMs know and what people think they know
finding: Users overestimate how often LLM answers are right when shown default explanations. Matching explanation length to the model's real confidence narrows the gap.
numbers: 301 participants across Experiments 1 and 2; 40 questions each; multiple-choice and short-answer.
limits: About monitoring and communication, not strategy knowledge. Only abstract and methods read.
agent_relevance: Weak link to this subfield. Stated confidence and wording mislead readers; the class record should store measured hit rates, not wording.

source: Metacognition-as-Reward (2026) Reinforcing LLM reasoning via knowledge and regulation signals
finding: Uses the Schraw split directly: a rollout has a knowledge part, a regulation part and an answer, and RL rewards all three. Gains over final-answer-only reward on 22 benchmarks.
numbers: Up to 7.7% over base model (science), up to 11.0% over vanilla DAPO (rubric benchmark). Long-context process analysis: +17.2% knowledge monitoring, +10.7% regulation fidelity, +9.8% final answer. Qwen3.5-9B OOD average 75.1%, +2.4% over base.
limits: Preprint, 2026, not independently replicated. Gold knowledge units are annotated per item. Gains are up-to maxima.
agent_relevance: First work that trains on the knowledge/regulation split. Only partly read; no clear ablation shows the knowledge part alone is what helps.

source: Cross-study pattern: self-chosen strategy vs imposed strategy (synthesis of b13, b12, b14)
finding: Across three studies, procedural knowledge is easy for LLMs (follow the named method), while conditional knowledge (choose the method) is the weak part. Learned or external selectors help; self-selection by a weak model does not.
numbers: Phi-4: free choice 47.2% vs forced strategies 45.1% to 49.0% (b13). GPT-3.5 MRP 0.433 vs best fixed SPP 0.469 (b12). SMART gain falls 15.2 to 3.5 points as base accuracy rises (b14). Oracle gap 35.7 points on TruthQuest Phi-4 (b13).
limits: Synthesis by the research agent across different tasks and metrics; not a pooled estimate.
agent_relevance: Design rule: keep selection in program code, fed by measured per-class results.

source: Gap note: no behavioural test of conditional knowledge found in opened sources
finding: In the Colombian MAI paper the declarative, procedural and conditional subscales are tested only as first-order groups under one knowledge factor, and that structure failed. No opened study tests whether conditional knowledge predicts picking the right strategy in behavior.
numbers: Higher-order model CFI .84, RMSEA .11, N=528.
limits: Absence of evidence in the sources opened; a wider search might find behavioural tests (for example strategy-choice tasks in children).
agent_relevance: Open gap. Our agent can test it directly: measure whether the record's picks beat a fixed operator per class.

source: Hartwig & Dunlosky (2012) Study strategies of college students: are self-testing and scheduling related to achievement?
finding: Students often prefer weaker study strategies such as rereading and know less about self-testing. Self-testing use is related to grades. Not opened this session.
numbers: No numbers recorded because the text was not read.
limits: Paywalled; fetch attempts failed. Claims here are from prior knowledge. Listed for a later pass.
agent_relevance: Human analogue of poor conditional knowledge: knowing a strategy exists is not knowing when it works.

source: Veenman, Van Hout-Wolters & Afflerbach (2006) Metacognition and learning: conceptual and methodological considerations
finding: Review arguing that metacognitive skill is general and teachable, that on-line measures beat questionnaires, and that training works best when embedded in the subject, explained, and long enough. Not opened this session.
numbers: No numbers recorded; about 1,420 citations by Crossref.
limits: Claims written from prior knowledge of the paper, so treat as unverified.
agent_relevance: Backs the point that questionnaire scores (MAI) are weak guides and behaviour logs are better, which is our design.
